expectedBehavior: R1 is limited to the authorized v2s AI-first and governance root and creates no R2 fresh-session evidence, W1 runtime, business OpenAPI, database migration, dynamic environment, seed or reset action, or Git write.

The project-memory denominator is exactly six named kernel entries and five named routed entries; every assertion has one exact owning path and literal heading, sourceRefs is only the sorted unique assertionSources path set, and semantic source substitution fails even when the replacement heading exists.

SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and Stop execute only the commands registered in .codex/hooks.json, obey closed input, output and exit contracts, never let Prompt query or inject source candidates, and scope Stop only to the named session and its explicitly owned managed runs.

The target Roadmap, immutable transfer receipt and expected ACTIVE Registry are fully checked under a non-current candidate root; final Roadmap and receipt bytes publish while the Registry remains non-authoritative; Registry activation is the only owner switch and happens last; failed readback deactivates Registry before restoring any other current file.

The transfer evidence is non-circular: sourcePreparedHash freezes before an immutable implementation closure, the candidate receipt binds that closure and contains candidateVerifiedAt but no transferredAt, and the separate immutable post-transfer closure records the observed activation time and active resolver hashes.

The dependency registry begins with modules and edges empty, has closed exact shapes for COMMAND, SCHEMA_FK and TASK_READ, independently proves owner direction, projects separate COMMAND and SCHEMA_FK DAGs, and permits TASK_READ cycles without granting write, import, transaction, lock or FK authority.

HANDOFF has exactly seven approved rows and exact id-to-trigger mappings, with every decisionSource represented as a reopenable repository-relative path plus literal heading; Heritage has exactly four read-only repository records and thirteen selected all-v2 assets with no write, runtime or build fallback.

R1 closure accepts only the independently enumerated R1 path allowlist, permits exactly the two module-dependency policy contract files, rejects every other contract/runtime/business path, separates business and cleanup evidence, and binds self-review and the final Dexter/Claude packet to explicitly named immutable artifacts.

The three production hook registrations, five-second timeout, closed stdin/stdout/exit contracts, session and managed-run schemas, ownership boundary and production-command fixtures are exact.

Source never preclaims GO and is never written after sourcePreparedHash.

Module.commandApiPackages and ownerSchema provide independent direction oracles for COMMAND and SCHEMA_FK. Exact semantic identities, target existence, separate DAG projections and reverse fixtures are specified.

The Heritage denominator is exactly four repositories and thirteen hash-bound all-v2 assets; the other repositories are explicit empty future-only selections and every repository is no-write, no-runtime-fallback and no-build-fallback.

The immutable candidate receipt explicitly omits transferredAt and records only candidateVerifiedAt. The separate post-transfer closure is the sole owner of the real activationObservedAt value.

adversarialChecks: Implementability: the repository entry, five skills, three hooks, context scripts, exact eleven-memory inventory, routing vocabulary, generated indexes and checker paths are specified without requiring the implementer to choose a denominator.

Security and authority: project memory and skills are repository-owned, Prompt cannot inject source or code, unknown routes fail closed, Stop cannot traverse or attach unrelated session/run state, and R2/W1 plus Git remain forbidden.
Production consumer: lifecycle fixtures must parse .codex/hooks.json and invoke its actual registered commands, so helper-only green cannot replace client-path evidence.

Evidence oracle: deleting COMMAND_REQUIRED_TRANSACTION and preserving assertion text while rebinding it to a non-owning heading independently fail; the corrected cross-document assertion classes have exact owning headings.

Plausible wrong mutation: a provider executable, global skill path, Prompt SOURCE output, route drift, extra active memory or substituted owning source is rejected while the aligned repository-only deterministic path remains valid.

Implementability: source preparation, prepared current files, non-current complete candidate, non-owner publication, atomic Registry-last activation, readback and Registry-first rollback form one exact serial protocol.

Authority leakage: the ordinary resolver returns no active target until the already verified ACTIVE Registry bytes are published last; source never claims GO and cannot be written after sourcePreparedHash.

Failure recovery: candidate failure publishes no authority, interruption after Roadmap/receipt publication leaves Registry non-authoritative, and post-activation failure first removes resolver visibility before restoring prepared snapshots.
Evidence oracle: sourcePreparedHash, final target, immutable receipt, expected Registry and Heritage hashes are independently bound; R1-to-R2 continuity and copied all-v2 program state are rejected.

Plausible wrong mutation: target hash drift, two active owners, an all-v2 current owner, early Registry activation, receipt transferredAt, or post-candidate receipt mutation each violates an explicit final oracle.
Implementability: the empty dependency truth, closed module and edge variants, seven complete HANDOFF rows, four Heritage repositories and thirteen selected assets are fully enumerated.

Owner and transaction: COMMAND.apiPackage must belong to toModule, FK objects must belong to their endpoint schemas, COMMAND and SCHEMA_FK use separate DAGs, and TASK_READ cannot grant write or transactional authority.
Data evolution: R1 honestly creates no schema or migration and invents no module or edge; future reconciliation keys are exact without pretending runtime observations exist.

Evidence oracle: correct and swapped command directions, FK inversion, duplicate identity, missing target, illegal command/schema cycles, legal read cycles, vague triggers, unresolved source anchors and omitted Heritage assets are independently discriminated.

Plausible wrong mutation: a syntactically valid COMMAND owned by fromModule, a compound WHEN_NEEDED-style trigger, a Heritage writeBack flag or an extra current-truth repository all fail despite appearing structurally complete.

Implementability: the aggregate order and exact create/update/delete/retain boundary identify the pre-transfer implementation closure, candidate transfer receipt, post-transfer closure, self-review and Claude handoff finalization points.

Evidence ordering: implementation closure freezes after sourcePreparedHash and before candidate construction; candidate-bound bytes never mutate; activationObservedAt exists only in the post-transfer closure created after active resolver readback.

Cleanup and exclusions: the exact baseline-diff allowlist permits only the two dependency policy contract files and rejects apps, libraries, database, migration, other contracts, business OpenAPI, DEV/runtime output and any active managed resource.

Review freshness: Codex self-review binds the immutable implementation closure, while the Claude packet binds the post-transfer closure, immutable receipt, implementation closure and self-review; any later mutation makes a named hash stale.

Plausible wrong mutation: a third contracts file, app directory, migration, stale self-review hash, mutable receipt, nonzero resource, cleanup failure or simulated post-activation failure without Registry-first deactivation is rejected.

conclusion.summary: The current R1 implementation-facing design is implementable and independently falsifiable. The last memory provenance, closure allowlist, evidence finalization and activation-time issues are closed without weakening the Registry-last authority boundary or expanding R1 into R2/W1.
conclusion.authorizationBoundary: GO permits the already authorized R1 implementation only. It does not authorize R2 fresh-session acceptance, W1 runtime or business code, DEV, seed/reset, any destructive data action, or Git stage/commit/push/branch/worktree. Dexter and Claude must still review the completed R1 implementation and its immutable closure evidence.
